name: Non-syndromic urogenital tract malformation of male

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and imaging criteria for non-syndromic male urogenital malformations

criteria.description: Presence of congenital structural malformation of the male urogenital tract confirmed by imaging or surgical exploration
No associated syndromic or systemic abnormalities on clinical and genetic evaluation
Exclusion of acquired or infectious causes of urogenital tract anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital structural malformation of the male urogenital tract without syndromic features and confirmed 46,XY karyotype
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies on exclusion of syndromic and acquired causes and confirmation by imaging and genetic testing.

pathognomonic.notes: Abnormal ventral placement of urethral meatus
Failure of one or both testes to descend into the scrotum

common.notes: Penile length significantly below normal for age
Retrograde flow of urine from bladder to ureters
Recurrent infections secondary to structural abnormalities

occasional.notes: Benign cystic formations in the epididymis
Dilation of renal pelvis due to urinary obstruction
Reduced sperm production in adolescence or adulthood

imaging: Ultrasound demonstrating structural abnormalities of testes and urinary tract
Voiding cystourethrogram showing vesicoureteral reflux or urethral anomalies
genetic: No pathogenic variants associated with syndromic conditions
Possible involvement of genes regulating urogenital development (investigational)
other: Physical examination revealing hypospadias, chordee, or cryptorchidism

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic or syndromic features
Absence of congenital anomalies on imaging

redFlags: Bilateral cryptorchidism with absent testes on imaging
Severe urinary obstruction causing renal impairment
Presence of ambiguous genitalia suggesting syndromic disorder
references: Orphanet: Non-syndromic urogenital tract malformation of male, ORPHA:182121
Genetics in Urogenital Malformations, Journal of Medical Genetics, 2022
